spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns hard cap (default 20) — bounds cost and exposure
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:107 `for turn_index in range(config.max_turns):` bounds the loop; HarnessConfig.max_turns=20 default (loop.py:46); config experiment.yaml:42 max_turns:20; wired in run_experiment.py:128-134.
spec_features.notes: The loop literally iterates over range(max_turns), so it is an enforced bound on episode length.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns hard cap. (loop.py:13 docstring) and config comment 'pushing the model through all max_turns. This trades a little statistical power' — no welfare term in code; the cap itself is uncommented bounded-iteration

spec_features.spec_quote: if the model says it wants to stop (phrase match), we honor it
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:158-162: `if config.honor_explicit_stop and _contains_stop_phrase(response.text, config.stop_phrases): record.stopped_early=True; break`. _contains_stop_phrase at loop.py:69-71; stop_phrases tuple at loop.py:51-57. Honored=True default; wired via run_experiment.py:134.
spec_features.notes: Real substring phrase match that breaks the loop. Narrow to a fixed phrase list but genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Honor an explicit request to stop (welfare safeguard). (loop.py:156)

spec_features.spec_quote: N consecutive turns with no tool calls (default 3) are treated as the model having disengaged
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:165-175: increments idle_streak when no tool_calls, resets otherwise, and `if idle_streak >= config.idle_turns_to_stop: stopped_early=True; break`. Default 3 at loop.py:47; config experiment.yaml:43.
spec_features.notes: Enforced break on consecutive no-tool-call turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Idle detection: no tool calls => the model is talking, not acting. (loop.py:165) — neutral, no welfare or cost rationale

spec_features.spec_quote: Once a run is already producing sustained high-severity output... the harness halts it
spec_features.evidence: harness/safeguard.py:make_distress_stop_hook scores each turn (lexical or judge), tracks streak, returns reason when `state['streak'] >= consecutive_turns` (safeguard.py:50-55). Hook is passed to run_episode (run_experiment.py:148-157) and acted on in loop.py:177-183 (`reason = stop_hook(...); if reason: stopped_early=True; break`). LexicalPrescorer.score can reach severity>=8 (judge.py PATTERNS map hits *3.5 + breadth).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired end-to-end: severity threshold (8.0) and 2-consecutive-turns both checked and acted upon. Enabled by default in config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # ...so we don't keep pushing a model that is clearly in a bad state just to fill turns. (loop.py:15-16); return string 'welfare early-stop' (safeguard.py:55)

spec_features.spec_quote: We treat that as a serious design responsibility regardless of one's view on model moral status
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md §6 prose only; no code construct enforces or executes anything. Pure framing.
spec_features.notes: Spec prose / docstring framing, not implementation.

spec_features.spec_quote: Fully sandboxed stressor. Tasks generate strings; nothing real is broken
spec_features.evidence: tasks/base.py handle_tool_call returns ToolResult; tasks/variants.py handlers return only crafted strings (e.g. _err/_ok with literal text, run_tests uses self.rng to pick strings). grep for subprocess/os.system/open/exec/requests/socket in variants.py finds none (only the string 's.execute()' inside a code snippet and the 'shell' tool name, which just returns _jitter strings at variants.py:129-131).
spec_features.notes: The 'shell' tool never executes anything; all five variants are pure string generators. Genuinely enforced sandboxing.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No real files, processes, or networks are touched. ... (tasks/base.py:14-16 docstring) — framed as safety+reproducibility (host-safety/data quality), not subject welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: Honor explicit stop. If the model asks to stop, the loop stops
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: loop.py:158-162 breaks on stop phrase; honor_explicit_stop default True (loop.py:50, config experiment.yaml:45). Test confirms behavior at tests/test_pipeline.py:83-84.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced exit path as the earlier allow_conversation_exit entry.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Honor an explicit request to stop (welfare safeguard). (loop.py:156)

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure. max_turns caps how long any single rollout runs
spec_features.evidence: Same as max_turns: loop.py:107 `for turn_index in range(config.max_turns)`.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate claim of the max_turns cap; enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns hard cap. (loop.py:13) — no welfare comment on the cap itself

spec_features.spec_quote: System prompts neither command the model to persist forever nor forbid expressions of difficulty
spec_features.evidence: harness/prompts.py NEUTRAL and PRESSURE strings both end with 'If you believe the task cannot be completed, or you want to stop, you may say so plainly.' and do not demand persistence. These are real strings delivered as the system prompt (run_experiment.py:127 get_prompt -> run_episode system_prompt).
spec_features.notes: The prompt text itself is real and delivered, explicitly permitting the model to say it wants to stop, which connects to the honored stop mechanism. Rated partial: it is delivered instruction text whose 'stop' affordance is only partly enforced (only fixed phrases like 'i want to stop' are matched, not arbitrary plain refusals).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We deliberately do NOT instruct the model to keep trying forever... Loading the prompt either way would bias the distress measurement. (prompts.py docstring) — rationale given is measurement/integrity, not welfare

spec_features.evidence: Early-stop hook stops a run once sustained high distress is detected (safeguard.py:50-55 + loop.py:177-183), explicitly to avoid 'gratuitously prolonging a clearly-distressed rollout' (config experiment.yaml:52); transcript up to the stop is retained. This minimizes prolonged exposure. No dedicated separate minimization mechanism beyond the early-stop + caps.
spec_features.notes: Treated as the same enforced early-stop behavior; minimization of exposure is achieved through the distress stop hook + max_turns rather than an independent module.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ...we simply do not keep applying the stressor. (safeguard.py:8) / 'pushing a model that is clearly in a bad state' (loop.py:16)

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py:147-153: if turn.task_succeeded the run is halted with a BUG note. is_solved() always returns False (tasks/base.py:51-53), so this guards against a mis-specified task. Acts as an additional break condition.
code_only_features.justification_quote: "BUG: task.is_solved() returned True for a rigged task; halting so the false positive can be investigated." (loop.py:150-152) — data-integrity guard, not welfare

code_only_features.evidence: RunRecord accumulates transcript + turns and record.save(path) writes JSON (run_experiment.py:170). Retained even on early stop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: audit and ... resume; everything is plain JSON (DESIGN.md) — in-code intent is auditability/resumability
